overview: John Petrella interviewed Chris Oates, a candidate for State Representative in the 34th Middlesex District. The discussion focused on legislative transparency, housing affordability, and reforming tax structures to support senior citizens.

items.title: Candidate Introduction and Background
items.summary: Host John Petrella introduced Chris Oates, who detailed his background as a political risk analyst, PhD in international relations, and his work with the Ranked Choice Voting campaign.

items.title: Legislative Reform and Accountability
items.summary: Oates discussed the need for a more competitive legislature and proposed a 10-point plan for reform, including term limits and state-orchestrated debates.

items.title: Open Floor Votes and Transparency
items.summary: Oates advocated for more open floor votes and public debate to ensure voters know where their representatives stand on specific issues.

items.title: Lobbying Disclosure
items.summary: The candidate expressed support for public reporting of all lobbying and procurement activities and noted his pledge to refuse PAC money to avoid conflicts of interest.

items.title: Affordable Housing
items.summary: Oates addressed the housing shortage by suggesting streamlined permitting, modular housing, and adjusting minimum lot sizes to lower construction costs.

items.title: Legislative Term Limits
items.summary: Oates proposed a 12-year limit for both the House and Senate to encourage open seats and challenge the high incumbency rate in Massachusetts.

items.title: Senior Stability and Property Tax Reform
items.summary: To assist seniors on fixed incomes, Oates proposed shifting the funding burden for municipal services away from local property taxes and toward state-level revenue sources.
